instruction: Do the new shift rules in Major League Baseball make the game more exciting?
reference: Prior to this season, Major League Baseball(MLB) allowed infielders to shift based on who was at bat for the opposing team. The shift simply means that the defending infield could load a certain side of the infield. For example, the shortstop could move to where the 2nd baseman normally is positioned and the 2nd baseman might play in shallow right field. The 3rd baseman would occupy the left side of the infield. The theory behind this shift strategy is based on advanced analytics used in the game of baseball. Using a spray chart to determine where a hitter normally puts a ball in play and with what type of pitch thrown, the defending team would shift to cover more of the playing field and therefore increase the chance the defending team would record an out based on this strategy. It was increasingly used over the last 3-4 years and some argue that employing the shift decreased the number of hits and runs scored during a game. The downstream effect of this made for a lower scoring affair and a less exciting game for a fan base that is increasingly younger and looking for more excitement during baseball games. One argument for allowing the shift is that hitters, being professionals, would adjust and try to beat the shift by hitting a ball away from the shift or hitting to the "opposite field." Hitters answer to beating the shift was to increase their launch angle and play for the home run. While the home run was an important run scoring mechanism, MLB decided to outlaw the shift from defensive strategy for the 2023 season. Hitters refusal to adjust to the shift led to this decision by MLB. The concern was games were not action packed enough and ultimately MLB would continue to lose popularity by its younger viewers, opting for other sports like Basketball, Football, or Hockey to spend their money on. No longer can you sift defensive players. The rules for this season are there must be 2 defenders on each side of 2nd base and their feet must be on the infield dirt as the pitch is being delivered. The hope is more hits will be produced, more runs scored, and an increase in fan approval created. The early opinion after the first week of the MLB season is that the games are proving to be faster paced with more runs and all around action created.

instruction: Provide instructions on making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich
reference: Making the perfect peanut butter and jelly sandwich is part art and part science. One must must be judicious in the quantity of ingredients while ensuring proper coverage to ensure each bite is equal to the one before and after it. Here, both measurement and distribution of ingredients serves as the scientific aspect of constructing your delicious and timeless lunchtime meal. Jars of peanut utter suggest a serving size as 2 tablespoons, which, when applied to the critical soft white bread, may prove too much to hold and cause soak through or tearing of the bread. We think 1.5 tablespoons is the proper amount to ensure there is coverage of the bread slice to the crust without compromising the integrity of the bread. Jelly application is even more precarious, as it holds more fluid and can soak through the bread quicker; equally, jelly has a tendency to congeal. To ensure proper application, heat the jar of jelly closer to room temperature if refrigerated, then apply using a clean butter knife or small spatula. Again, one must ensure it reaches to the crust and is evenly distributed. Once you have complete coverage of peanut butter on one slice and jelly on the other, place the peanut butter side of the first slice on top of the upward-facing jelly slice. This ensure none of the jelly slips or drips. Once together, gently compress the sandwich. Slice delicately from one corner to the opposite corner. Gently press the crust edge of each triangle, and plate for serving.

instruction: Imagine you are the last person on Earth. Write a diary entry describing your thoughts and feelings.

Yes, I am the only person around in this world. Does this make me happy or sad, you ask? I am conflicted, to be honest. As an introvert, I always wanted solitude and peace. The ability to be myself, to not just think my own thoughts but act like no one was watching. And yet, now, when I really can do this (believe me, no one is watching me, or even the security tapes!), I long for a voice to hear and for someone to talk back to me, see me act stupid or act out my weirdest thoughts, and in general just listen to me. But, there is no one. And this scares me, as well. Why am I writing this down, when I rarely, if ever, read you back? It is, probably, with a hidden hope that someone some day will read it and understand my thoughts and ideas without judgement. If no one ever will read it, because there is no human left on planet Earth, why am I writing this even? I always read (and scoffed at) the books telling me "Man is a social animal" - I felt they did not refer or apply to me me. And now, dear friend, I have realised a little too late in life that it wasn't the books that did not recognise me. Rather, it was I who didn't understand myself. Farewell and adieu!

instruction: Why should people drive cars with manual transmissions?
reference: People should drive cars with manual transmissions because it forces drivers to be more engaged while driving and lowers the incidence of distracted driving, making it the safest choice overall. Environmental concerns about fossil fuels aside, one of the biggest issues with driving today is distracted driving. With improvements in cruise control technology and other driver assistance functions like lane keep assist, cars are taking over more of the driving process than ever before. While the intent is to make it safer for drivers, it also has the unintended consequence of making easier for drivers to be distracted. Cars with manual transmissions not only force greater engagement and focus, but they are also either incompatible with, or only compatible with lesser versions of, certain driver assistance features like adaptive cruise control because lowering the speed while not being able to change the gear (which is manual) could cause the car to stall. Paradoxically, by increasing the required inputs and decreasing the number of driver assistance features, driving a manual transmission car is safest.

instruction: Write me a recursive function for calculating the nth fibonacci number
reference: Below is a recursive Python function fib(n) that computes the nth Fibonacci number. This is split into a base case and a recursive case. The base case is given by the fact that the first two terms of the Fibonacci sequence are 0 and 1, so fib(0)=0 and fib(1)=1. The recursive case is given by the fact that the nth Fibonacci number f_n can be written as the sum of the previous two Fibonacci numbers, so f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2}. Putting this all together, we get ``` def fib(n): # base case if n == 0: return 0 if n == 1: return 1 # recursive case return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) ``` This will correctly calculate the nth Fibonacci number for nonnegative integer inputs n. However, recursively calculating Fibonacci numbers in this way takes exponential time in the value of n, so this code may be very slow for large inputs. It could be improved by memoizing previous results, or using a non-recursive approach. Simple iterative approaches can solve the problem more quickly, and closed-form expressions for the nth Fibonacci number exist and are even faster to evaluate.

instruction: How do I make a perfect grilled cheese sandwich?
reference: Step 1. Select a cheese that will melt well. Parmesan, for example, is not ideal for a grilled cheese sandwich. Cheddar, Havarti, and Colby Jack are all cheeses that taste great and will melt. Step 2. Get two slices of bread, preferably not too thick; typical store-bought sliced bread like sourdough, potato, and white make adequate grilled bread. Step 3. While you are assembling the sandwich, heat a shallow pan over medium-low heat on your stovetop. Step 4. Spread some mayonnaise on the inside of each slice of bread. Sprinkle some garlic powder over the mayonnaise -- this gives a little extra flavor that one might not expect from a grilled cheese. Step 5. Layer the cheese between the slices of bread. Don't put too much cheese on it, or it will leak out of the sandwich when you cut it! Step 6. Assemble the sandwich and put a thin layer of mayo on the outside of each slice. Step 7. Lay the sandwich inside your heated pan. It should sizzle immediately. Wait two minutes and check to see if the cheese is melting. If the bread is browning too quickly, turn the heat down. When it is adequately browned on one side, use a spatula to flip it over to grill the other side. Step 8. Once your sandwich is grilled to your liking, turn off the stove and remove your sandwich from the pan. Slice diagonally and serve with a bowl of hot tomato soup. Enjoy!

instruction: If you found yourself washed up on a deserted tropical island with no hope for immediate rescue, what would you do?

Find fresh water and someway to hold it (open coconut shells / fashioned palm leave bowls etc) - DO NOT DRINK IT until you boil it first over your new fire so you mitigate the risk of getting sick. Before your first nightfall with secure fire and water taken care of, build yourself a make shift shelter so you are protected from the elements and yet to be discovered critters. Day two, focus your energies gathering food (coconuts / seaweed / clams etc) so you keep your energy high. Once your very basic needs are met (shelter / water / food to survive), its time to fashion a fishing pole and a sharp spear out of bamboo so you can fish and hunt for birds to expand your food sources. Day three, focus your energy on building yourself a more permanent shelter. Explore the island for wood and rock sources; along with large palm leave you can fashion rope from. While exploring your new home, look for caves and / or places where you could construct a tree fort so you can improve your protected living space. Week 2, once your new living quarters are secured and you have sustainable methods to care for your basic needs, climb to the highest point of the island and look for nearby islands / land and any indication of human habitation. While searching for these indicators, assess methods of island escape to get through any surf and start tracking wind and weather patterns daily so you can get a feel for the seasonal rotations. Week 3 +, dedicate 3-4 hours a day to building signal fires and SOS stone messages that overheard planes may be able to detect. It is also important to manage your mental health and track daily changes so you keep your sanity in check as you adjust to the new reality. Create a way to chronicle your experiences. One day you will escape your island and can sell your story to Hollywood. Of course, if you never do escape, you will at least have the comfort of leaving something behind for eventual discovery of proof you did survive the incident that landed you on this island.

instruction: Describe a plan for training to compete in a long distance gravel cycling event, including nutrition, preparation, and recovery requirements. Your plan should include a timeline and be relevant to someone who works a full time job.
reference: General guidelines call for four rides a week but no less than three days a week. Your overall weekly training time commitment will vary, as you professional demands permit, but will increase as you get closer to your event. In the early stages of your training, expect to spend about six to eight hours on your bike each week. Many part time riders with full time work commitments will be looking at a few weeks of eight to 10 hours of riding time, the bulk of which will come from your long rides. During the week, your rides will be shorter, but a little bit harder. Typically those who work and train for long distance riding events perform measured short distance rides in the early morning before work or mid-afternoon during breaks. On the weekends (or whenever you have days off), they’ll be longer and a bit easier. Recovery and nutrition will be important for non-ride days Most people in training benefit from a recovery drink after hard workouts, eating plenty of fruits and veggies, drinking lots of water, meditating, and practicing yoga, along with flushing her legs with self-massage tools and foam rollers. It is important to get a good nights sleep. Bedtime is prime time for bone, muscle, hormone, and immune system restoration. Do allow for seven to eight hours of sleep per night. The following lead time is generally required for each time of event: If you are training for event in the 50- to 75-mile range, you'll want to begin training at least six to eight weeks in advance. If you’re training for anything in the 100-plus range, allow 10 to 12 weeks. If you’re preparing for an event in the 200-mile range, begin training 16 weeks out. A typical training week should include the three types of targeted training, plus one or two days of cross training (strength and core training) and rest days Before your event, you will want to be within 75% to 80% of miles and elevation required for the event with the final week before your event tapering off to rides at 20-25% of length compared to the event.

instruction: Does parallel universe really exist?

There are several evidences for parallel universe, such as Hawking radiation, which says that anything going into a black hole might end up in another universe. or the gravity waves act oddly and deviate objects from their orbits, possibly due to the influence of parallel universes. This idea of multiple universes has been proposed in various fields of science, including physics, astronomy, and even psychology. For example, Stephen Hawking was the leading theoretical physicist who advocated multiverse theory. Curling up by the gnarled roots of a blackened tree, my tears’ floodgates suddenly opened. I muffled my sobs as much as I could. “You should not dally, Miss.” I bolted upright at the voice. It was not the Witch’s screech, but a deep baritone. Even so, my heart trembled with fear. “Who’s there?!” A stag stepped out from the underbrush. It was not a tall one and was clearly advanced in years, but he looked me square in the eyes. “You cannot stay here. If you do not keep moving, the Witch’s minions will snatch you. Come.” Though skeptical, I had few options. I staggered to my feet and followed the greying stag deeper into the forest. The canopy blotted out all but the faintest glimmer of sunlight. I was nearly ready to collapse by the time he stopped. “You are safe for now. You may rest with us.” To my surprise, I saw the dim figures of many animals around me. Not only deer but squirrels, boars, rabbits, beavers, and more. They chittered amongst themselves excitedly. At length, the stag spoke again. “Did you truly escape the Witch’s Tower? Under your own power?” It took time to find my voice. “Yes,” I said meekly. “It took a long time of looking for opportunities.” “Then you may be the one who was foretold. The great champion who will be our avatar in the human world.” Suddenly the creatures draped a heavy cloak over my shoulders and an antlered helmet upon my head. “You will defend the forest from those who would do it harm and enlist the good peoples of the human world to battle evil. You, young lady, are the Thicket Warrior.”

instruction: Write a short story about Penny and the Pirate. Penny is a girl who finds her grandmother's old wooden talking chest in the attic filled with gold. It’s the pirate’s voice. reference: Penny cherished her grandmother's attic more than anything in the world. It was her haven, where she would indulge in hours of exploration, delicately handling the exquisite relics that adorned the space. Her favorite thing over there was the old wooden chest nestled in a dark corner of the room. The chest would beckon to her, even when she was far away, drawing her closer with an irresistible magnetic force. One rainy day, Penny finally resolved to unveil the chest's mysteries. She lifts the lid of the chest, and suddenly, she can’t believe what her eyes can see. It’s filled with shining gold. The mixed feelings of surprise and happiness that she felt were short-lived – she heard a deep and gruff voice emerge from within the wooden chest. ‘What do you think you're doing?’ The chest growled. Penny was jolted so intensely that she almost slammed the lid shut. Yet, her inquisitive nature egged her on, compelling her to stay put and listen. The voice persisted. ‘You have no right to open this chest. It belongs to another.’ Penny's confusion mounted. How could the chest belong to anyone else? She tried to question the voice about the rightful owner but held back. Instead, she listened, captivated by the voice that began to weave a tale. The voice belonged to a pirate who had sailed the seas eons ago. The pirate stashed his treasure in the attic. He collected everything he had ever made and saved in his life inside this chest. Nobody in the world could know the location of his hidden and gold-filled chest except him, not even his crewmates. The voice cautioned her that the riches were cursed, but Penny was skeptical. She put her hands inside it and filled them with gold. Her eyes followed her hands until she pulls them up to see the gold shine in the light. For weeks, the chest continued to talk to Penny. It spun stories of amusement and intrigue, and the two grew intimately close. Whenever Penny felt low or lonely, she would clamber up to the attic, nestle by the chest, and listen to its tales. Slowly, Penny began to realize that the chest was more than a voice. The pirate's spirit was trapped within its walls, imprisoned there for centuries.

instruction: I need a list of 3 or 4 Polish scientists, in numbered order based on when they were born, focusing on those that worked between the 15th and 18th centuries. I need names, birth and death dates, education and what they accomplished. Leave a space between each one.
reference: 1. Michael Sendivogius was a Polish alchemist and an early worker in chemistry. He worked on developing ways of purifying and creating various chemical compounds, including various acids and metals. Sendivogius discovered that the air that we breathe contained a substance he called "food of life," later named oxygen, by heating saltpeter. He was born on February 2, 1566, in Lokowica, Poland, and died in 1636 in what is now the Czech Republic. He attended or visited many European universities including the University of Vienna, the University of Altdorf, the University of Leipzig, as well as the University of Cambridge. 2. Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was born in Poland on May 24, 1686, to a family of German descent. As a glassblower, he invented the thermometer by putting mercury in glass. He also developed the Fahrenheit scale for measuring temperature. Fahrenheit was interested in science and he began studies and experimentation by contact with other scientists including Ole Rømer, Christian Wolff, and Gottfried Leibniz and by visiting Berlin, Leipzig, Dresden, and Copenhagen. He was very knowledgeable in chemistry and in 1718, he began lecturing in Amsterdam. He was named a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1724. He died in 1736, at the age of 50. His funeral was held at the Kloosterkerk in The Hague. 3. Wojciech Jastrzębowski was born in Poland on April 19, 1799. He passed his exam at the Warsaw Lyceum and became a scientist, naturalist and professor of botany, physics, zoology, and horticulture at the Polytechnic and Agricultural and Forestry Institute (Instytut Rolniczo-Leśnyin) in Warsaw. Jastrzebowski wrote on the study of humans at work and was the first person to use the term "ergonomics". He died on December 30, 1882. 4. Jędrzej Śniadecki was born in Poland on November 30, 1768. He graduated from the Chief Crown School in Krakow and in 1797, was named Chair of Chemistry at the Main School in Vilnius Lithuania. He was the first to show that rickets developed from a lack of sunlight. Śniadecki wrote a book, The Beginnings of Chemistry, that was so important that it was used in Polish universities into the 20th century.

reference: The day had gone much like any other, with patrons sitting around the tavern, talking about the harvest, their wives, or anything else they wanted to socialize about. Ale was shared, toasts were raised, and the atmosphere was quite rustic and charming. However, this day the tavern was a little more packed than usual; a traveling bard had come to visit the village. He worked by playing music for tips and a free night's stay. The bartender was happy to have him, he needed for little, was polite, and played his lute well. The bard was happy for the hospitality, and the chance to play his music for an audience. But occasionally, with so many people and with so much alcohol around, tensions would rise and a fight would be inevitable. Two big men, both who worked with lumber for the village, seemed to lose their sense of reason and civility, as they both stood up and started accusing each other of something. At first, they were mostly ignored, as people were known to get a bit rambunctious around this time. But then one of the men slammed his fist right down the table, splitting it in two. Everyone stopped to stare at the arguing men, and even the bard stopped his tune as all eyes were clearly on these two. The shouts started to get louder, although nobody had a clue what had gotten them so upset in the first place. Just then, the bard recalled a song his mother played for him as a child, that always brought calm to his heart. And so, he started to strum a new tune, one that filled him with a sense of nostalgia, and that started to draw the attention of the tavern goers once more. The shouting men didn't respond at first, but after a few seconds their shouts stopped, and they looked over at the bard as he played a beautiful, almost otherworldly melody. The anger drains from their faces, replaced by tears that start forming in their eyes, and they sat down in their chairs, enthralled by the melody. Finally, the bard finished his song, and the whole tavern, including the once-angry men, applauded the performance. The bard gave a bow, the men looked over at each other and forgave each other with a handshake, and peace returned to the tavern once more.

instruction: What is the difference between a panster and a plotter? Is one better than the other? I am writing a blog post on it, but for right now I just wasnt some brief tips so I can research further. For now, just a couple of paragraphs is fine, I just need something to get me going.
reference: A panster writes "by the seat of their pants". They start with a general idea, or maybe even just a character, and just let the story go where their imagination goes. Stephen King, Diana Gabaldon, and George R.R. Martin are great examples of pansters. A plotter is a writer who outlines the story before they write a word of it. The most famous plotters are J.K. Rowling and James Patterson. Then, there are authors who combine a bit of both, like Agatha Christie. As far as what is best, it really depends on both the writer and the story. A panster may write an entire first draft without outlining. A plotter usually outlines everything first - settings, characters, scenes - and then starts writing. The drawback to pantsing is the writer might box themselves into a corner and need to re-write. The drawback to plotting is that as the story continues, the characters begin driving the story and tweaks need to be made. Genre is also a consideration, as it is much easier to pants science fiction than a mystery.

instruction: The European Union uses carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2-eq) in their emission trading system to penalize the use of non-renewable energy sources. Is the CO2-eq a good pollution metric or does the system need improvement?
reference: The use of CO2-eq as a pollution metric in the European Union's emission trading system is a step in the right direction, but it may not be the most effective way to penalize the use of non-renewable energy sources. CO2-eq measures the total greenhouse gas emissions produced by a specific activity, including not only carbon dioxide, but also other greenhouse gases such as methane and nitrous oxide. This allows for a more comprehensive approach to addressing climate change and reducing emissions. However, the use of CO2-eq as a sole metric for penalizing non-renewable energy sources may not fully address the environmental impact of those sources. For example, the burning of fossil fuels not only releases greenhouse gases, but also air pollutants such as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. These pollutants contribute to air pollution, which has direct and immediate health impacts on local communities. Therefore, while the use of CO2-eq is a good start, the system could be improved by incorporating additional metrics to address the full range of environmental impacts of non-renewable energy sources. This could include measures such as air pollutant emissions and the use of scarce natural resources. In conclusion, the use of CO2-eq as a pollution metric in the European Union's emission trading system is a positive step, but it is not enough on its own to fully address the environmental impact of non-renewable energy sources. Further improvement is needed to ensure a more comprehensive and effective approach to reducing emissions and mitigating the impacts of climate change.

Unfortunately, the only way to form and retain friendships is to spend time with another person. If your work takes up a large amount of your waking time you will find it comparatively difficult to make friends with people outside of work. I am assuming that you are a man since men in particular form friendships around common interests. Are you sure that you don't share common interests with your coworkers? Ask about their interests and try to understand what they care about. Even if it turns out that you don't share common interests they will probably appreciate that you're trying to learn more about them. They may also feel the same way you do and want to form friendships with other people but simply not know how to make the first step. Good opportunities for casual conversation include lunch breaks and coffee/tea breaks. To find friends with shared interests in particular you can try to attend real-life events that revolve around said interests. You probably wouldn't feel comfortable at a rock concert with lots of people and loud music but how about something like Dungeons & Dragons where a small group of people plays a game in a quiet room? Maybe there are clubs for the discussion of books or anime that you could join. In any case, if you invest time and effort into making an activity fun for other people they will want to spend more time with you (but this of course requires time and effort). Finally, you mentioned that you don't have many friends - but this means that you still have some. Keep in touch with them and share what is happening in your lives with each other. Maintaining a friendship is much easier than forming a completely new one and you will feel more comfortable around people that you already know compared to strangers.

instruction: Back in 4th grade you wrote a short story and as a joke you posted it online. Years go by and when you go to check on your old posting you see that it has started it's own cult....

Fifteen years ago, on the hospital stretcher, Jax's mother's last words were to eat bananas " and this," she pointed to her failing heart, " will never happen to you." Jax was nine at the time. But he listened to her. He only ate bananas. She passed away from a failed heart a week later. In Ms. Dogger's 4th grade class, he scribbled out a four line poem: *Mommy said to eat bananas* *Mommy said to please be smart* *Mommy said she's sorry, son* *Bananas would have saved her heart* In his basement, now, as an 24-year-old, Jax opened his laptop and typed in the address. His boyfriend Hans watched over his shoulder. Ms. Dogger had liked the poem so much she put it on a website, www.bananas-of-the-heart.com. The site came up, but Jax didn't recognize it. The design was cleaner and fresher; it had a minimalistic yellow and white theme. In the center of the screen was written, " BANANAS DOn't JUST CHANGE YOUR LIFE, THEY SAVE IT." He snorted. " What is this?" He clicked over to the blog. The last posting was dated yesterday. " Hans, get a load of this." Hans frowned. " Is this the same site? Click the About page." Jax clicked *About* and the screen was covered by an image of an old, thin, and sickly looking woman with yellow skin smiling while playing in a sea of bananas as if she were in the McDonald's ball pen. The first line read, *Hi, I'm Joanne Dogger, founder of Bananaism. * Hans and Jax looked at each other. " Damn." They read on. *Bananas cure sickness and disease, clean your soul, and deliver happiness. * " She's crazy," said Hans. Jax said, " Apparently, she's not the only one." At the bottom of the page, it said, " Join me and 34,341 banana believers." " Do we dare click around?" " If that *appeals* to you," Hans let the pun slip out. Jax elbowed him in the chest. He clicked *Story* at the top of the page. An image of his poem from his 4th grade class appeared on the screen. He gasped. Right below the image, the words said, *Where it all began*.

She was flanked by two young men -- her brothers -- in canvas suits. Marc and Paul Green carried small guns at their sides, their hair slicked back. They looked almost dead-eyed as if they were not seeing the world fully. Or seeing beyond it. Donovan stood up. He approached Julia, watching her adjust her red ponytail. She had something written on the back of her neck.Kanji. Perhaps she had been to the Chinese district? Tattoos were still very common in some parts of the New City. Marc and Paul had the same designs though the font seemed to be different. Julia brought a hush to the group. She didn't say anything, setting down her bag on the floor and pulling out a device. Donovan knew what this was, he had paid for all the parts. Julia was going to save the world, the right way. She would be the criminal mastermind, take the fall for a cause she believed in. " My name is Julia Green and I am from the Wedge." She lifted her right hand and shook her bangles. Two people in the room followed her motion, their own bangles clicking together. Donovan felt like his mouth was dry. Something was wrong.

instruction: [OT] Readers of /r/WritingPrompts. What's more important to you while reading a story: Content, or Context? Does layout, style or grammar affect your opinion? Why?
reference: There is a balance point between content and context I'd think. I don't care much for Hemingway; his books read like mummy dust: dry. On the other hand, *Finnegans Wake* has so many multi-lingual puns and cultural references that it is almost impossible to thoroughly enjoy. When it comes to sparser prose, I think *All Quiet on the Western Front* is just about the most perfect story, the bleakness of the war is apparent in the prose. I love it. On the other end of the spectrum, and the end which most would agree I belong to, there is more competition. I really like S M Stirling's style, it's descriptive and colorful, and he can paint a fight scene very well without turning it into purple prose.

instruction: Earth is sucked into a parallel universe through a worm hole. There are now two earths in orbit around the sun. Contact between the two planets are established.
reference: Finally, the communications are ready. Those who are left on this world finally have some hope. In a way, it will be a comfort, to finally discuss with Earth Prime (We decided to call the other Earth " Prime" it is their universe, after all) what our place in this new universe will be. The team flips all the appropriate switches, and the comms link is established. But something is wrong - there is just static. Each outpost we reach, all we hear is static. Choking back panic, the lead technician checks his calculations. He knows there is life on the planet, the orbital scanner confirmed it. He sees his simple calculation mistake, and the team sighs in relief. We make a simple adjustment, and the sound focuses and clears. It wasn't static. It is so much worse. Each post we contact, each continent, the entirety of Earth Prime, it is all the same. Screams. Our link to the past, our guide for the future, is drowning in endless, terrible screaming.

instruction: [CW] " A flash of light, a puff of smoke, and she was gone. "
reference: Her eyes searched over the audience. Applause filled the room, reverberating off of the walls and bathing her in their adoration. This was it. This was the moment she had been waiting for. She dreamed of standing here, her arms open and taking a bow, ever since she was a child. “ Thank you. Thank you so much, ” she shouted out to the audience. And then she waved her hand through the air, performing the last trick for the night, the first night of many to come. She threw the ball down at the ground triumphantly. A flash of light, a puff of smoke, and she was gone. Her assistant came running up to her backstage. “ Wow, that was amazing, ” the assistant exclaimed! “ I know. I can ’ t believe they actually liked it so much, ” the magician said in disbelief. “ With that kind of audience and that level of excitement, I think we ’ ll be performing here long into the future. ” She sat in a chair and contemplated the entire evening. Finally, she was satisfied with her life. She was where she was meant to be, and she was going to enjoy putting on a show every week. -127

instruction: You are a teenager with the ability to measure how " Dangerous " people are on a scale from 1 to 10 just by looking at them. A normal child would be a 1, while a trained man with an assault rifle might be a 7. Today, you notice the unassuming new kid at school measures a 10.
reference: " GET AWAY FROM ME!" I screamed, " HAVEn't YOU DONE ENOUGH?". I gathered up my things and slowly backed away towards the door. It was my fault, really, messing with a ten. You see, I could always see numbers. Obviously, I'm not talking just about the ones you learn in math class. No, I'm talking about a rating system, of how dangerous a person is. A 0, is like a baby; very low chance of causing harm. A 7, is like a desperate robber; not knowing what he will do with that knife in his hand. I have never met anyone higher than a 7 in real life before, not yet at least. I was putting my stuff back in the locker that day. It was pouring outside, i mean, what do you expect during the monsoon season? Surrounded by 2s and 3s, I was relaxed. Thinking to myself, when was the last time I saw a 1. And suddenly, I felt a hand grab my heart. Instinctively, I whirled around. And there she was, pretty like the first snowflakes during winter. So smile-invokingly innocent looking. So.. Perfect. The numbers fleeted away, and I couldnt see anyone else for a while. And I noticed something, she was wet. Poor soul didn't have an umbrella. I rushed over with a towel, and introduced myself, and there, in her eyes, was the reason why my heart stopped. Ten. " You have to give it a shot!" I argued with myself, " you've never seen a ten before! What if, what if it means she's perfect!" " What do you mean what if she's perfect? She IS perfect! But a ten definitely means danger, right?" " You don't know that.." And I stepped into the best relationship of my life. Getting there was not easy, not by a long shot. I mean, the world is not stupid. Everyone could see how perfect she was. That cute smile, insightful comments, knowing how to do what she loves. But when you get there, wow. Things were going great. And one day, after two children and a dog, it all went bad. I got home early from work that day, still as in love as the day I met her. But.. There were clothes on the floor, not mine. A laptop bag, not mine. And a guy in bed with her, not me. The same feeling from 18 years ago came back. That hand gripping at my heart. And that's why, you never mess with a ten.

instruction: You are part of a small colony of humans 100 years into a 200 year interstellar mission. Due to the time passed, technology has allowed a new mission to exceed yours, and it sails past your ship but can not make contact
reference: **Exodus Log # 481 - Rotation # 20** *2132; 98 Years after Mission Start Date* Most of the crew is still in the Freezer. Well, actually, everyone except for me is still asleep, decided not to wake up the other Technician's after I saw the transmission from Earth. Unfortunately for everyone on board this ship, our leaders back on Earth have decided to send another mission to ION-4. They decided to dub it Exodus-2, as if the four hundred souls they sent on this mission have already returned or are already dead. We are not dead. And we are still 102 years from our destination. According to the transmission, we should be seeing Ex-2 any day now, even though they only left on their mission fifteen years ago. Technology has advanced at a rapid rate since we all left. Although we've been gone for 98 years, technology has moved jumped about 200 years. And unfortunately for us, they didn't account for this when they sent Ex-2 into the stars. Unfortunately for us, we'll get to watch Ex-2 fly by and reach ION-4 79 years faster than us. By the time we get there, everyone on board Ex-2 now will be dead, or in the final days of their life. And we'll be reaching a colony of their children. We'll be the eldest people on the planet, clocking in at 200 years older than anyone else. I, for one, am not looking forward to this. And I for one, am going to keep my crew in the Freezer for a few years longer than they anticipated. It's against regulation, but when the people who sent you on this mission 98 years ago, send a newer, fancier, and more technologically-advanced ship on the *same exact mission*, well, I think we can let regulation slide for a bit. I'm going to do the rounds, check on everyone's status, then watch Ex-2 flyby us. Without saying a damn word. Ex-2, if you're receiving this somehow, or hell if Earth can send this to you, I only have one thing to say. Tell your kids we're on our way. And we won't forget about them.

instruction: Stars have brilliant deaths, large explosions given a beautiful name. Men are granted nothing so glorious.
reference: They've been talking about it for billions of years now. The fact that we've made it this far is a credit to our race. We've seen glorious scientific triumphs, the fall of many great civilizations, and even times of peace. Today though, none of that matters anymore. The Sun was always only a battery, never a generator. No matter how many brilliant minds we put to the task we could never change that fact. Everyone around the planet is coming to terms with the end of the world in their own ways. Some are rioting. Others are at home quietly with their loved ones. Even more have ended their lives already in fear of what is about to happen. But none of that matters anymore. *Stars have brilliant deaths, large explosions given a beautiful name. Men are granted nothing so glorious. *

instruction: [TT] You are the Leader of an Elf Squad tasked to bring coal to naughty children. The price of coal has gone up. You need to find a suitable replacement
reference: (little bit of swearing) Elf Squad leader, Jolly's my name Would you like to know how I shot up to gain all this fame? I started the idea of giving out coal, disappointing naughty kids, now that was my goal. Come every Christmas, we still carry out this plot the very first person to receive coal had the name Scott. Santa came in and busted down the door, spilling his milk and cookies all over our floor. " This is no good! No good!" " Stop worrying Santa, you never should!" Santa explained the whole mess of a situation. I ordered all the elf's to come listen, and abandon their workstations. " Elf's, we can't afford coal!" the crowd responded, " What, you must be a troll!" " I assure you I'm not one, for don't I have pointy ears and can build a water gun? Unfortunately, I fear we have more pressing matters, we are on the brink of a global disaster. We must find a replacement for coal by tonight, before Santa takes off for his annual flight. Does anyone know of something?" honestly all I could think of was the Hot line Bling. " Remember that thing we saw on Reddit?" an elf said, " We can build it using only a thread!" That was a perfect thought. " Elf Sam, that's the best idea you ever brought! Everyone, it's time to build!" I then pulled to side the elfs which were more skilled. " Look, I request you make as many as you can it doesn't need to look as good as Santa when he was a young man." ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 8 hours has past, and we were done at last. Santa walked in and said, " Ho, ho hold up. Whats this?" " This? This is a sight of bliss!" " Did you just mold things with bull-shit?" " It's all we could find on the threads at Reddit, besides, you never said we couldn't, and it's too late too argue, so we really shouldn't. You need to go deliver these presents to everyone living in houses, apartments, or even tents!

instruction: A man walks in to a bar for his usual drink, but his life is forever changed the second he takes his first sip.
reference: *This is my first ever submission - have always been a reader rather than a contributor but this WP intrigued me. Any constructive criticism would be welcomed! * * He'll never forget that moment. That second when everything changed. It was gradual at first, a sip of his favourite drink, a notion that something wasn't quite right, a blurring of the senses. 'Strange', he thought.'This is my first drink of the day, I shouldn't be feeling so fuzzy'. Slowly it dawned on him, this feeling wasn't borne from being drunk, or even tipsy - he had just assumed that was what was happening to him because his world had become blurry and unfamiliar. It was only once he came to this realisation the fear hit in. Being drunk? That was something he new how to handle, but this... this was new, it was scary and most worryingly of all it was unknown. He blinked furiously but the blurriness stayed, resolute, unmoving. He blinked again. Nothing. Just a vague sense of fog, of blackness seeping in. Could it have been the drink? Surely that was impossible... but then, what else could it have been? Suspicion set in and he glanced over at George, the bar man. He shook his head slightly -'no, it can't have been anything to do with him, George was his friend, wasn't he?' Starting to panic now he stood up, uncertainly at first, clutching at the bar and trying desperately not to let the worry show in his face, to take deep, calming breaths and sort out the myriad of un-scrambled thoughts that were colliding inside his head, behind the very eyes that were, inexplicably, failing him. Blink. Nothing. Blink. Still nothing. The darkness grew heavier, more dense.'It's OK, he thought to himself, I'm fainting'. Eventually, the darkness consumed him, but he never hit the ground.

instruction: You thought learning the recorder in elementary school was some stupid music thing teachers made you do. It turns out they were training you for something else.
reference: We all thought the recorder was just some stupid instrument the teachers made us learn to " expand our experiences" We were wrong. No one could have predicted the war, but some how our teachers knew. All of that year learning, practicing, mastering the recorder would come back and save us. The machines, monsters, I don't know what to call them, they were invulnerable. Bullets could not stop them, explosions would not slow them down. We all thought hope was lost, but then the 9th grade Travis school kids came out. Formed rank and played. It was ugly, it sounded horrible, and it looked bad. But the music, no the noise, it overwhelmed our adversaries. It started to make them bleed and eventually weakened them and then we were able to win. That's why we learn to play the recorder. As a nod to our heritage and the war. " But mr Thomson, why doesn't Timmy have to learn" " Oh his parents gave him a note"

instruction: Our cause is righteous and just. We will not falter
reference: I recited the words, " Our cause is righteous and just. We will not falter," although I am the last one. For centuries I've stood guard in the same room. Many have tried to reach me, but all have failed. I remember the blistering sun of the desert, and the cool breeze of the Mediterranean. All else is becoming a faint memory. My daily routine of overseeing my treasures. That's what every man and woman have called the objects in my room. Little do they know that the word should be singular. Oh the treasures of this plain are worth quite a bit, but it is only the treasure of salvation that they should truly seek. I gaze into the small pool of water located in the center of my chamber. The echoes of another man screaming. Prey to another device. Maybe he doesn't know to kneel, or maybe he doesn't know how to spell. Some simply fall to their doom. More echoes. I've grown numb to the sounds of men dying. Even that of women. All I seek is the one to relinquish my duty. Footsteps. Those I have not heard since the time of Napoleon. In comes a man with a fedora on his head seeking the cup of a carpenter who took his name from the family dog.

instruction: War has been raging for years upon years now. You are a reporter embedded in a famous military unit among your newest allies in this war, humanity.
reference: " Centauri News Conglomerate is broadcasting live from the MDU's most decorated commander's ship, the Endurance. We will be making contact with the Gaddian main fleet at any moment. Commander Alexandr, what should viewers expect to see in the next few minutes?" *The Commander waves to his adjunct whilst continuing to inspect VIDAR screens and issue terse commands. The adjunct steps into the foreground. * " This will be a historic day in the Nuebarr-Gad conflict; we will intercept their main fleet during its attempted jump to sector 2B, catching them completely unprepared and striking a decisive -- --". " Multiple detonations off the port side!" **" Damage control to corridor Monsoon" ** *The audio feed is saturated by the sound of alarms and tortured metal, while the video feed shows sluggish MDU cruisers being picked off one by one by the nimble Gaddian torpodeo ships, their engines disabled, allowing them to be hit by the enemy battleship's barrages. The heavily armoured MDU ships take a long time to go down. * " Sir, we are detecting no other MDU lifesigns, we are the only ones left!" " You can activate the hyperdrive now, it has been long enough" *Once the Endurance is safely in hyperspace, the sullen reporter advances on Commander Alexandr and starts an emotionally charged rant: * " We were promised hundreds of ships, and a swift victory, what are you doing? You promised us your ships could not be touched by Gad weaponry, that their ordinance was swift and deadly. This defeat leaves the route to our homesystem -- -" *Alexandr roughly shoves the tiny Nuebarrian reporter to one side, and stoops menancingly to address the camera, a malevolent smirk creeping across his face. * " Those were not our *ships*"...... From the Nuebarrian homeplanet, in the middle of the day, two bright flashes could be seen: first, one close to sector 2B, followed an hour later by one in the Gad controlled sector designated " Tartarus"....... " This reporter is pleased to announce that the main enemy fleet will be stuck near sector 2B for at least 2 more days. During that time, our MDU allies will strike at production centres and supply routes left vulnerable. The tide of war has turned, thanks to Centauri News Conglomerate playing a key counter-intelligence role, and our MDU allies taking advantage of the enemy's confusion."

instruction: You've been dead for 67 days. You awake to the entire world watching the first human revival. Your revival.
reference: I knew when they'd brought my body back. The golden fields had faded, the feeling of overwhelming peace had vanished, and the pain had begun again. It felt like I spent an eternity in the darkness, certainly far longer than I'd spent in that glorious paradise. You don't realise how painful living is until you've stopped doing it. The awakening was sudden, my eyes snapped open as if from a dream. Hands pressed me back into the bed, and more hands removed the tube I was choking on. Shutters began to click the moment I'd opened my eyes, shouts of surprise from people around me. I would later learn I'd woken up before they had intended, the world's press taken by surprise around my hospital bed. In those first few moments the camera flashes were blinding and the noise overwhelming. Everything stopped though, when I screamed. At first the noises were just screams of pain, but they began to grow more coherent. " LET ME GO BACK!" And then darkness again. (This is my first time posting something like this, please be gentle.)

instruction: When you drink from a water fountain, and you unknowingly become immortal. How did you find out and how did it affect your live?
reference: *F**k! This again. * You see, a funny thing happened to me on my way to work this morning. Well I say funny but it actually is quite the opposite, a gust of wind caught me mid umbrella-unfolding and then next thing you know, I'm in the middle of oncoming traffic and bam! I'm back in this cursed corridor, in my old awful high school next to the blasted water fountain. Have you ever been caught sneaking around a high school? During the school day? The day I slipped in the shower found me on the register, and not the kind you'd expect to find in a school. And oh, look! There is good old Mr. Jefferies and yup, he is calling the police. Oh and would you look at that it's recess. ^ (Hi kids! Don't do drugs!)... God I wish I did drugs. Y'know, I hate that water fountain. I hate that Mr. Jefferies and I hate the fact I was on my way to work as a photographer. *Yes you can confiscate the damn camera! * Well at least I know how I'm getting out of prison.

instruction: You've finally done it: unquestioned world domination. The planet is entirely under your control. Now what?
reference: ... I've been laughing for the last two and a half hours straight, and I can't remember why. I just keep thinking " world domination, finally", and then giggling to my self. I am almost out of breath, getting dizzy, " look up, look up". I turn my head head to see a control panel with red lights blinking, and then it's all familiure, but my head is foggy. A straining gaze towards the panel reads oxygen critical. Panning to the left I notice blood, " is that my blood?" There is a shape in the corner looking lifeless. I immediately feel a sinking, cold, feeling of regret, as a red stale light beams through the two foot squared port hole. With nothing but barren terrain on the other side. I remember. The Mars project... I had a friend here.... I slip again into hysteria, smile, shed a tear, and as I pass out, mutter " world domination".

instruction: At the end of the year, a superhero receives a box in the mail from an anonymous journalist. Inside are hundreds of flash drives, filled with obituaries of people that the hero failed to save. At the bottom of the box, there's a note that simply reads, " The price of living a normal life. "
reference: It took me hours to gather each of the obituaries. The flash drives weren't all that expensive, and each one held a few thousand obits. This so-called " hero" thinks that he's perfect, but he's just as flawed as everyone else. What I didn't expect to see what a reply. A small note appeared on my doorstep. There was no address but with the hero's insignia on it, the note couldn't have come from anyone else. " It took some time to find you, but I have my journalistic resources too. If you thought that there were a lot of people that I couldn't save, wait until you see the number of people that I won't. I quit."

instruction: [FF] " The place where no star gave light "
reference: A rouge planet. Lost in the cold, empty cosmos. The nearest nebulae was lightdecades away, there was no star here. No source of external heat, no supernovae nearby to end it's solitary existence. It was dark, and drifting. Beneath the crust, over millions of year, life had found it's way here still. It evolved and thrived near the vents spurred active by the hot iron core deep inside the planet. Over the countless number of years it became aware, discovering love, gods and loss. Scientific thought came next, followed closely by curiosity. The studied, postulated, and guessed under hundreds of miles of thick rocky crust, living out their days to understand what was beyond the roof of their existence. Still hundreds of miles below the surface, they worked to penetrate the inner layers to discover what was " out there." Time passed and lives were lost in their journey to understand what was above until finally, they broke through. It was then that those first explorers lost faith in their gods. They realized they were Alone, they understood they were drifting and if life existed outside of their planet they would before they were found. This knowledge would destroy them. They would arrange an accident, hoping to cause loss of public support to cease the studies. They would sacrifice themselves to spare the shame of a long sought after dream.They would retreat inside their planet, back to the warmth of understanding and forget their loneliness. Theirs was the place where no star gave light.

instruction: Write the letter that you always wanted to, but never did.
reference: Dearest whomever is left, I don't know when in my " life" you'll be reading this or what the circumstances have been. I am sure of how I feel, always have, and always would have. Since you're reading this Its certain that I have finally been able to take control and I'm no longer with you. It wasn't out of sadness or depression. It wasn't because you all weren't fantastic. I enjoyed every moment of you. What's a million sunrises without a final sunset? Don't be sad for me and don't take it out on yourselves. I loved every moment even the bad parts because they gave way to better times. I waited until Tony went because that responsibility was mine to shoulder. No one else needed to carry that weight. Some of you may have noticed me acting odd lately. Going out of my way to fix things with people, pay my debts. Hand out apologies to some and offer forgiveness to others. I finished shows and stopped starting new ones. I've run my gas tank dry and donated any funds I may have had left however meager they may have been. When you guys talk about me, don't talk about the darkness" in my life. Don't discuss how I went. Share the lessons we learned together. The fun we had and the adventures we went on. Know I killed my self as an Atheist so I don't expect anything. I went smiling because I finally had the freedom to do what I wanted and this is It. I wanted control. ALWAYS have. I hope that P outlived me. I hope she was happy in life and know that my final thoughts where of her. I never forgot the promise I made. Make sure she knows that. Fuck you everybody goodnight! Signed A happy man who died in love P.s. You know what to do with my hdds, ssds and endless crates of composition books........no peaking.

instruction: A prehistoric monster pursues its goal in anyway possible to receive three dollars and fifty cents to pay for its greatest desire.
reference: It was about seven or eight years ago. It was my duty. I needed this. How else will I pay for my daughter's college tuition? Three dollars and fifty cents left... I don't have a job, I don't have much in the bank, I have no living family or friends, and my wife left me many a year ago. I needed to get up the mountain. Her life depended on it. It was a hard, hard ordeal. There were wolves, there were hunters, there were bears, even. But I kept going, it was for my only child. I kept climbing through the bloody thing... Time could be running out... I got over the mountain, it was midnight. I saw a lake and was dehydrated. I guess I'd take a swim, so I got in. I saw an elderly couple in a boat. I don't know why I'd ask them, but I knew I needed to... " What do you want from us, monster!?" I bent down and I said, " I-I need about tree fiddy."

instruction: A butterfly flapping its wings in China causes a storm in America. What motivations would a butterfly have for doing this?
reference: As the butterfly sat, perched atop a daisy, soaking in the consequences of what it was about to do, there was only one thought running through it's little mind. *For the souls of all the bees you've slain, trees you've slaughtered and fish you've farmed, I shall do unto you what you've done unto them. * It can't be said that the butterfly's wings made a sound. It can't be said that one could even detect a shift in the air. But that single flap of that single butterfly's wings had started something. Something was on its way to America. Retribution.

instruction: In 1907 Vienna Academy of Fine Arts rejects Young Adolf Hitler twice and soon after he survives four different assassination attempts by time travellers. Confused Hitler is convinced that its his art is what the world fears.
reference: There is no more doubt what I must do. But I'm not sure why I have to do it in the first place. The rejection by the Academy, twice, stings, but to be hunted down for what is just a few paintings? What is so wrong with them? What is it about them that would cause these time travelers keep coming back to kill me? I'm just an ARTIST. I want to have people enjoy my art. More importantly, I want to enjoy making them. Instead, I" m hunted. But no more. I've survived this fourth attempt to murder me. I will continue to survive, for I must do what is now, clearly apparent to me as being necessary. The world *will* like my art. I will see to it. It is my *destiny*.

instruction: Berlin, 1943. You're a Jew who has been successfully keeping a low profile while working as a clerk under the 3rd Reich. You just found out you've won a contest to spend the day with the Führer.
reference: " Herr klum as an appreciation of the great work you have being doing to help the third reich, you have been rewarded to a dinner with the führer herr hitler himself" " Ahh wundervoll" I replied I could fell the sweat about to leak from my forehead. My knees would have gone weak if I wasn't sat at my desk organising the train timetable for platform 4 Berlin Central station. A few days later... I boarded my train on platform 3 (the destination was undisclosed so the english couldn't find adolf) and entered a light sleep. A few hours later I was woken by some ss guards and escorted to the venue. It had many workers in the grounds surrounding, and the excitement of meeting hitler blurred my thoughts. It only took a few moments for me to relise auchwits wasn't a hotel, it was a death camp. They'd got me!

instruction: The person sitting next to you on a plane leans over and says, " Don't ask me how I know this, but this plane is going to crash before it reaches Newark. "
reference: I leaned against the window, trying to drown out the whines of the young children in front of my with music, when I felt a tap on my shoulder. I pulled my earphones out, sighing lightly. “ Yes? ” “ Don't ask me how I know this, but this plane is going to crash before it reaches Newark." He replied, his face completely serious. I stared back at him for a moment, my brows furrowing. “ What? ” I said. I felt the blood draining from my face. He nodded grimly. “ But don ’ t worry, I have a plan. There ’ s some parachutes in the- ” I cut him off before he could finish. “ I thought this plane was going to New Mexico. ” Well, this was going to screw up my schedule, I thought glumly as I listened to him detailing his survival plan.

instruction: Follow-up: You are a compulsive dancer. Anywhere there is music playing you struggle to remain still.
reference: The disease began with me. As far as I know, I was the first recorded case of it. In the beginning, friends and family thought it was a joke. The doctors thought me a liar. There was no possible scientific explanation for a disease that would make one dance, of all things, whenever music was heard. It just made no sense. But when we discovered that it was contagious, that I spread the disease wherever I went, the doctors started studying me seriously. Still, at the time it was still just a passing curiosity, and no hindrance to everyday life. The unease began when it turned out that the spread of the disease started to accelerate. The doctors, through careful experimentation, discovered that the disease had a delayed onset upon exposure. That countless many may have caught the disease without displaying the symptoms became cause for concern, and the doctors started working towards a cure. Then, finally, the terror began with the soft humming of a pop song. The music was heard everywhere, even in enclosed rooms, seemingly without a source. The city, as one, began to dance a subdued little jig. Following that, Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. If you are unfamiliar with this song, it is an hour long, quite dramatic and powerful. Accordingly, the people of the streets waltzed, forcefully. Twenty minutes in, the streets were panting and gasping from exertion. At the end of the song, screams for mercy were heard across the city. At that time, whatever cosmic DJ that staged this impromptu dance party decided that the warm-up was over. It began to play its own unending mix of heavy metal and dubstep. And oh how the city learned to hate these two genres. Between the headbanging and moshing, the screams ended. There was no breath left in the people to scream. The city fell, one by one, out of heart attacks, strokes, exhaustion. The weakest among us died within half an hour of the mad dance. The strongest began collapsing after the third hour. And I? I managed to crush the auditory organs in my ears through a particularly inventive method of headbanging, along with parts of my skull. And as I lay bleeding and dying, I looked out into the crowd and cursed the cruel and twisted world that would come up with the terrible and silly idea of compulsive dancing.

instruction: " What happened to me? Were you here the whole time? "
reference: I think, deep down, I had thought I would never see her again. I realise that now as she stands before me, her grey eyes sparkling like they always did before. There's a swelling in my chest, the familiar surge of overwhelming love and deepest sorrow that always came to me in those many quiet moments when I thought of her. Only now it threatened to consume me. My eyes are so blurred with tears that I can barely see, yet I make out her hand reaching towards me. Without hesitation I take it. It's now I notice the gentle smile on her face, filled with familiar love and warmth. But her eyes... her eyes are darkened with a heavy sadness. And for a moment, it frightens me. I squeeze her hand more tightly as slowly fear and realisation begin to take hold and a memory forms in my mind... It was dark. The light from the streetlamps reflected in the wet pavement and I remember thinking in my own way it was somehow beautiful. Behind me there were footsteps. Quiet at first but steadily they became louder. I knew what would happen before it did. And as the now deafening steps crescendod, I braced myself and prayed I was wrong. I already know the answer, but now I've finally found my voice, I whisper " Grandma, what happened to me?" A beat passes by in silence and slowly she hangs her head and closes her eyes. She stays like this for a moment. When she eventually looks up, I see her eyes have filled with tears. It seems she does not have the words to tell me. A new question comes to me. And suddenly this one feels so much more important than the first. " Were you here the whole time?" Her face breaks into a loving smile. " Yes my beautiful girl. Yes I was"

instruction: [OT] Ask Lexi # 14 - Writing Believable Characters
reference: Didn't see it mentioned, but it's also important to explore a character's morality/ethics. Especially when writing an antagonist. Too often, people just write the bad guys as two dimensional Disney villains. They're bad because they're evil and evil because they're bad. And they will always say they are the villain with enthusiasm. But antagonists and villains don't think like that for the most part. Serious antagonists generally think what they're doing is right or have very realistic grievances with the protagonist that other characters in the story don't see. Magneto is probably one of the best examples of a character that plays the villain 99% of the time, but he is a very well-developed and believable character. There is ethical logic to his actions that constantly contends with the morals held by the protagonists.

instruction: A soldier in the heat of battle suddenly hears a voice that says " I am your child's imaginary friend. They have sent me to protect you in your greatest time of need. "
reference: Sergeant Coleman of the SAS had seen more than his fair share of battle. Yet ambushes were something even the elite can't always prepare for, his convoy as testament upon erupting in a series of explosions, but as it did, a voice rumbled into existence. " I am your daughters what you would call'imaginary' friend, and she made me promise to protect you, but it comes with a price" The voice was rasp but distinct, like it reverberated off the skull, intertwining with the rattles of gunfire and shelling. Coleman lay untouched next to the wreck of his vehicle, all occupants but him dead inside. Assessing the situation, their convoy came under attack from both IEDs and RPGs, with the explosions sending all vehicles in different directions, how he survived was a mystery. Doubled with hearing voices he thought he was dead, until a stray bullet glanced his arm and the white hot burn snapped him back to reality. " Wh.. what? Who are you?" " Who I am is not important, whether you wish to survive is. Three approaching your six, Sergeant" There it was again, whether it was the shell shock or his comms he couldn't tell, didn't care as he spun into cover as bullets whizzed by overhead, exactly where he was standing just moments before. " God damn it, I don't care the cost just get me out of here!" Assessing his options, Coleman saw two points of cover, sandbags or a building. Whilst blindly firing into the hills, the voice returned... " The building, might want to use one of those grenades of yours, run quickly now..." The voice trailed off as Coleman burst out of cover. The sand kicked and danced around him as he sprinted to the house and threw the frag inside. The resulting screams sent a shiver down his spine. How did whatever was helping him know? Bursting through the door the damage was already done, through the window he saw the sandbags get hit by a stray mortar, and explode upwards in a spray of sand and dust. " Delta squad under attack! I repeat!" The soft crackle confirmed his radios demise, just as an enemy silhouette materialised in front of the door with his gun raised. " Click, click, click..... Click" Four dead man's clicks? What were the odds? Coleman thought as he sunk two in his enemies chest. Suddenly he realised his wasn't the only presence. " You humans and your odds and chances, no you must live this day, for I forever keep my promises as you must keep yours..." It trailed off again, this time the vibration in his head seemed to finally leave, yet as he watched from the window the enemy emplacements misfired sending explosions all across the mountainside. Coleman reached for the photo of his daughter, and found a burn where her face used to be. " What have I done?"

instruction: In the near future, mankind explores the stars in search of life. Life indeed exists beyond Earth, but you, a researcher on a science ship, discover that all of the spacefaring alien civilizations died out. Curiously, their deaths seem directly linked to humanity reaching outer space.

instruction: “ I swear to god that painting is looking at me. ” … “ Don ’ t be silly. ” … ” SEE! There! It moved. ” … “ No, no it didn ’ t. ”

instruction: An alien race starts to colonize Mars. They completely ignore humanity on Earth and just go about their business.
reference: Part 1 of? The most concerning thing to the worldship Iki is that she didn ’ t recognise the civilisation currently growing on Mars. Or much about it, in fact; it was more alien than usual. As far as it could be said meaningfully on the topic, it was pre-metric, and didn ’ t have any Archons or Mechanotesseractoid brains. She pulsed at them in light, then radio, then neutrinos, then with a voxel wave. None of the signals were noticed or responded to. She did so again, shouting at them with every broadcaster, and there still wasn ’ t any acknowledgement at all. She briefly intercepted Earth ’ s outbound radio transmitters, as well as the Israeli prototype neutrino flinger that she was absolutely sure they shouldn ’ t have, and sent them some information from Earth ’ s direction. Still, absolutely nothing. Not wanting to bring Neptune ’ s eye to bear, she decided to abandon any harsher remote contact and brought down a physical probe. Specifically, two-hundred and fifty starfish nets. The first landed, and surveyed the landscape. It was, from the surface, the classic red Mars, with the exception of the grid of cubes in the distance. Some were still growing from the ground, bottom-down; others were fully grown, and glowed warmly, as one would expect from an area of habitation or power generation. The starfish net fluttered closer to the cubes. Externally, they were mainly featureless, with a few bumps and air filters around the shiny outside. It wandered around, looking for an entrance or exit, but there were none. A second net approached, and networked with the first, but their combined power still didn ’ t notice anything out of the ordinary about the cubes. They called up to Iki, who also failed to notice anything exceptional about them. After a few days of exploring, floating around the cubes, watching new ones be contructed then spring to life in the infrared spectrum all at once, progress in exploration had failed to be made. They were built in such a way that made them consistently secure to casual entry through the entire process; no visible gaps, even to the sensors of several nets working in concert, formed. The nets received a second command from Iki, permitting destructive exploration. One net immediately flung itself at the cube, and, tightly coiled, started burrowing through. The resultant reaction from the cube was exceptionally sudden, and comprised a multi-pronged memetic attack (of the standard, soft, and hard varieties, over multiple frequencies), followed by a conventional detonation restrained by force fields, followed by the space surrounding the net being partitioned and then voxelated, followed by something that Iki didn ’ t even recognise that caused storm activity on Neptune to flare up massively. Correction: the civilisation was most certainly post-metric, and destructive exploration was no longer taking place. Plenty of data was gathered there, though not all of it made a whole lot of sense.

instruction: You wake up in a dimly lit prison cell to find your cell door busted open, a pile of unconscious guards, a stuffed duck called Leeroy, the faint sound of Gangnam Style, and an absurd amount of blood on your hands
reference: " Why am I dreaming about Koreans?" I wonder as I regain maybe 1/4 consciousness from sleep. The air smells of ozone. And damp iron. I can hear a fluorescent light blinking rapidly on and off, trying to ignite the gas inside. Gangnam Style is barely making its way to my ears. " What the fuck?" I open my eyes. I'm staring at a ceiling I don't recognize. My blood runs cold and I sit upright with a jolt, eyes wide. I'm in a prison cell? I think. It's dark outside so no light is coming in from the slim window. The only light is coming from the faint and noisy flickering of a cheap fluorescent light above and what's coming in from the hallway outside. There is a steel door that is mangled to a degree that I can't fathom what in the hell could have caused its current shape. It's pushed inwards and the paint has come off where something struck it. Most of the paint that has come off has been replaced with what I'm sure is blood. A shoe lies in the view out the door from the bed. " So you're up." I let out a short scream like a girl and look around. There's no one. " Over here..." I look around. On the bookshelf is a stuffed animal. A duck. " On the shelf. Name's Leroy." " Yeah, I'm not fucking with any of this." I say and I lay back down, pull the sheets up and close my eyes. " Wake up, idiot!" A soft thud hits the floor. I open one eye and cast it towards the sound. The stuffed duck is on the floor looking at me. " Fuck off, duck." I close my eye again. " Leroy. And that won't work. Besides, we need to move before the guards who miraculously have survived regain consciousness and lock this place back down." " What?" The duck just blankly stared in my direction. " What?" No answer. I sit up. I pinch myself and recoil from myself as I notice blood *everywhere* on my hands and I hear a sigh from the floor. I look over at the duck. " Where am I? What's going on?" Still no answer. If I'm dreaming I'm not going to wake up by going to sleep in it so I swing my legs off the bed and stand up, bending down to pick up the duck I hear over the intercom, " All guards to cellblock B immediately. Secure the area at all costs!" I look at my door. Cell B-14. I poke my head around the corner of the doorway and onto the gangway. It is littered with guards and I can see flashlight beams far away heading towards me. Whatever is coming that way I have a feeling isn't going to be pleasant. " Run." Leroy says to me.

instruction: You're at a pub when you see an attractive woman sitting alone at a table, after you approach her and talk for a while you hit it off; only to find out that she is there to meet someone she met online.
reference: She batted her eyes at me, " You know, you're not bad." She spoke slowly so I would hang on every word, " In fact, you're doing really well at this whole'bar date' thing." It was good to hear, most times on these I've crashed and burned, " well, I'm good at a lot of other things too." I looked into her eyes and she looked back into mine. " I've heard a silver tongue can be very versatile." Un-fucking-believable. The woman he eyed was a voluptuous blonde with deep blue eyes and a clear complexion. She wore a tight dress that ended above her knees. She was the hottest woman at the bar. I had never had someone flirt with me like this on the first time meeting. Since the beginning, they had been flirting. Finally, I said: " You wouldn't even believe, it's mind blowing." " You know," she began, " I don't think you're a socially awkward penguin in the slightest." What. Roll with it. " Well, at the end of the day I am a human." " So, what, you told me you're bad at conversation. I think you're phenomenal. I only thought you were witty online, where everyone has minutes to think about what they say. Yet here you are, flirting like a champion. Are you gon na take me home, penguin?" "... Penguin?" " Tell me your real name, and don't say James Bond." " Joe." " Alright,'Joe,' I'll fold. I've been attracted to you before we even met here. The third night we talked I knew I was going to meet you. Do I meet your expectations?" Shit. She thinks I'm someone else. " Oh." I felt disappointed. This woman was drop-dead gorgeous and it had almost happened. " Well, listen, let me be honest- I don't think I'm who you think I am. " Well, you look like your picture. Thanks for not cat-fishing me, by the way. You're handsome." My god, I look just like this guy. " Well, I'm not the guy you met. Maybe a happy coincidence." " Oh my god," she said, " What the hell? Look at me, I'm hot! You're going to pretend this isn't you?" She pulled out her phone and looked through it a bit before stopping and turning it towards me. There, staring right back at me was my facebook profile picture.

instruction: The light glinted in the dirt, and there I found my future.
reference: Those nature walks were the only place where I could find comfort amidst the hubbub of my life. Between the escalating civil war with the rebels, my constant fighting with my girlfriend, and crushing pressure to perform well in my job, I was reaching the end of my rope. instruction: The protagonist often breaks the 4th wall, and so the narrator decides to break the 5th. Things are getting heated between the two.
reference: Yo, me again. It's the Protagonist. The guy who actually has to live out everything you people write. And, uh, this prompt is weird. See, oftentimes I *am* the narrator. This is one of those times. I guess I'm a masochist or whatever. So, enough talking to you, here's today's story. Woke up, drank coffee, went to the postmodernist dreamscape where all fictional characters go to perform their stories, yadda yadda. Anyway, so I was supposed to be acting out Deadpool today, but something went wrong. I was about to start, I had my lines ready. There was an excellent fourth wall break in my mind. I braced myself. It was time to run. I dashed forward with everything I had in me. The fourth wall was made of bricks, and it wasn't going to break easily. Still, I had to do it. The plot wants what the plot wants. As soon as I hit the wall, however, I knew I had made a mistake. This was not the brick of the fourth wall, or the curtain of the second, or even the bamboo paper of the first and third walls. As I crashed through the wall, splinters punctured my skin. The characteristic wood of the fifth wall gave way, and I entered a room of pure white. I fell to the floor, my vision blurry. I turned around to see the set disappeared, endless white filling my sight. In the distance I saw a blotch of brown, an oasis of color in this expanse of nothing. I made my way toward it with little hope of ever getting out of this realm. My vision cleared, and I saw a table. Upon it lied a pen and paper. A way out! I quickly scribbled down a story, crafting an escape from this nightmare. _______________________________________________________ Part 2 soon

instruction: [Semi-Historical] In 1787, Ben Franklin snuck a joke into the U.S. Constitution/Bill of Rights that was never caught and never removed. Centuries later, it inadvertently plays a major part in a Supreme Court decision.

instruction: You are a consort to the king of a kingdom at war. The king goes off to battle, but doesn't return. After the battle, two priests from a nearby shrine ask you to help them identify the king's body on the battlefield.
